sentences.text: In respect of an undisputed accident which has resulted in grievous injuries to the claimant, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,38,000/- and being dissatisfied, the claimant is in appeal.
2. The Neurosurgeon who was examined as PW2 has opined that the claimant had permanent global neurological disability at 75%.

The evidence on record indicates that the claimant suffered facial NC:
2024:KHC:51084 paresis and also hearing loss.
The certificate issued by the Neurosurgeon - Ex.P16 indicates that the claimant had obtained IQ of 46 which is in the range of below average intellectual ability.
The certificate also indicates that the claimant's language processing was inadequate and was very slow to respond.
In my view, in light of medical evidence, it would be appropriate to assess the whole body disability at 50% as against 20% assessed by the Tribunal.
3. The Tribunal has determined the notional income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/-

The claimant contended that he was working as a delivery boy and has produced the letter from the employer stating that he was not attending the work due to his illness and was hence removed from the job.
It also stated that he was drawing Rs.12,000/- as salary per month.
However, no bank statement was produced to indicate the same.

In such circumstances, it would NC: 2024:KHC:51084 be appropriate to adopt the notional income determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Sri Muniraju B R vs Mr Arun Kumar B N on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118698391/
2 Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2016, would be Rs.9,500/-.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the claimant suffered 50% disability, 40% requires to be added towards future prospects to Rs.9,500/-, which makes his income to be Rs.13,300/-.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.12,76,800/- (Rs.13,300 X 12 X 16 X 50%) towards loss of future earnings.

5. In view of the disability suffered by the claimant, it would be appropriate to enhance a sum of Rs.20,000/- awarded towards pain and sufferings to Rs.1,00,000/- and also to enhance a sum of Rs.15,000/- awarded towards loss of amenities to Rs.1,00,000/-.

6. Since the claimant was hospitalized for 22 days, it would be appropriate to enhance the sum of Rs.5,000/- awarded towards conveyance, attendant NC: 2024:KHC:51084 charges, etc., to Rs.30,000/- and to treat the laid up period as six months and consequently, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.57,000/- (Rs.9,500 X 6 months) towards loss of income during laid up period.
7.
The amount of Rs.2,22,000/- awarded towards medical expenses, being based on documentary evidence, is affirmed.

8. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:
